senses.gloss: (denom. of כֶּלֶב) [to make stitches resembling dog-bites (cmp. our ‘cat-stitching’),] to stitch, opp. to תָּפַר to sew in a workmanlike manner.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Moed Katan 1:8">M. Kat. I, 8</cite> (<cite ref="Moed Katan 8b">8ᵇ</cite>) <he>האומן מְכַלֵּב</he> Ms. M. a. Y. ed. (Mish. a. Babli <he>מַכְלִיב</he>) the professional tailor is permitted (during the festive week) to stitch (but not to sew); expl. ib. 10ᵃ <he>מפסיע</he> he makes wide steps (cross-stitches); (another opin.) <he>שיני כלבתא</he> (Ms. M. only <cite ref="K00687"><he>כַּלְבְּתָא</he></cite> q. v.) dog’s teeth, i.e. irregular stitches; Y. ib. 80ᵈ bot. <he>מפסיע</he>; (oth. opin.) <he>אחת אחת</he> each stitch singly. Ib. <he>הרוצענין מְכַלְּבִין</he> the saddlers are permitted to do dog-stitching.
